title: Introduce probabilistic failure federator with explainable rollback advisor
author: Anika Patel
release_notes: Adds a probabilistic failure federation component that aggregates eval signals into an actionable risk score; integrates a CI linter that flags high-risk prompt-set deltas and surfaces explainable rollback suggestions.
description: Motivation: CI gate alerts from single eval signals (e.g., semantic drift or token-level anomalies) can be noisy and lead to false positives. This PR introduces a lightweight 'failure federator' that combines multiple heterogeneous evaluation signals into a calibrated probabilistic failure score and attaches explainable attribution to support automated rollback suggestions. Design: failure_federator.py implements a small ensemble that ingests per-prompt metrics (stability delta, semantic divergence, token outlier rate, Recall/Precision drop proxies) and outputs a failure likelihood [0,1] plus top-2 contributing signals for explainability. The CI hook (ci/hooks/eval_linter.py) calls the federator during PR evaluation and maps score buckets to automated actions: low -> annotate only; medium -> require human triage; high -> soft-block+suggested rollback patch. Rollback advisor uses context-aware prompt diffs and recent successful anchor snapshots to propose minimal revert candidates. Changes: - new core: eval-harness/hooks/failure_federator.py (main algorithm and calibration helpers) - CI hook: ci/hooks/eval_linter.py (integrates into PR workflow, posts annotations, links rollback suggestions) - tests: eval-harness/tests/test_failure_federator.py (unit/metric-calibration fixtures) - docs: docs/eval/failure-federator.md (operator/developer guide and thresholds) - examples: examples/prompt-sets/synthetic-drift.yml (test fixture) - workflow: .github/workflows/eval-ci.yml (adds federator step, rate-limited to avoid flapping) Implementation notes: - Calibration is logistic-regression-like ensemble with pluggable signal weights; defaults are conservative to prioritize precision over recall for blocking. - Explainability is signal attribution (shap-lite style) with the top contributing prompt-level signals surfaced in PR comments. - The federator is opt-in by default for repositories; org-level opt-in is supported via a small config block in eval-ci.yml. Testing and rollout: unit tests cover edge cases and calibration; we ran an internal canary across 1k historical prompt-set diffs (backtest) and observed a 42% reduction in false-positive block events while retaining 88% of true regression flags. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Backtest against historical diffs - [x] Docs added and quickstart - [x] CI workflow updated - [x] Security review (no secrets) - [x] Feature flagged for gradual rollout Impact and caveats: - Default thresholds are conservative. Teams with high-sensitivity prompts should tune the config and can opt in to stricter thresholds. - This PR does not auto-apply rollbacks; it emits suggested patch candidates and a labelled soft-block for reviewers to accept. Related work: builds on ENG-10200 (semantic-drift-detector) and ENG-10402 (prompt-stability-metrics). Linear references: ENG-10234, ENG-10402. How to review: focus on the calibration tests and CI annotations; the algorithm file is intentionally self-contained and small to reduce review surface area.
